lines.text: Energy contracts: in your house you need electricity and usually gas.
You choose your own energy supplier [energieleverancier].

There are two kinds of contracts: a fixed [vast] contract (you pay the same amount for one or three years, even if prices fall [dalen] or rise [stijgen]) and a variable [variabel] contract (a different amount every month).
The energy bill: every month you pay an amount.
Once a year you get an annual statement [jaarrekening]: it shows how much energy you have used and how much you must pay extra or get back.
The meter reading: sometimes you must report the meter reading [meterstand] of your gas meter [gasmeter] and electricity meter [elektriciteitsmeter].
These are usually in the meter cupboard [meterkast].
You must do this when you move, when you switch to another supplier, and sometimes once a year — via the internet, by phone or on a card.
If you have a 'smart meter' ['slimme meter'], this is not necessary; you must first give permission [toestemming] to your supplier to read your energy consumption [energieverbruik].
Contact with the energy supplier: needed when moving or changing supplier.
In case of an outage/malfunction [storing] there is also a national outage number [nationaal storingsnummer].
First check what the problem is, but take no risk [risico]: a problem with gas or electricity can be dangerous.
Water: the water comes from a separate company [bedrijf] that serves your region [regio] — you cannot choose this yourself.
You have a separate water meter [watermeter] (usually in the meter cupboard) and report the meter reading once a year.

Saving water and energy [Water en energie besparen] is better for the environment and costs less: turn the heating off an hour earlier in the evening, set the heating one degree [graad] lower and wear warm clothes, turn lights off, shower shorter, turn the tap off while brushing your teeth, buy energy-efficient [energiezuinige] appliances (A-label; A+++ is the most efficient [zuinigst]), and wash at 40 degrees with a full washing machine.

Maintenance [Onderhoud]: in an owner-occupied home you pay the maintenance costs [onderhoudskosten] yourself, for example cleaning the heating boiler [verwarmingsketel] or hiring a plumber [loodgieter] or electrician [elektricien].
In a rental home the landlord does this; small problems (such as a new toilet seat) you solve yourself.
Internet, telephone and television: for this you choose a provider yourself; there are websites to compare [vergelijken] providers.
Insurance [Verzekeringen]: for living there are also insurance policies, for example home insurance [woonhuisverzekering] if you buy a house.
